purpose: Retire reconstructable closed frontend cursor entries under registry pressure without losing durable work or active task ownership
contract: Keep existing registry, worker, byte and deadline bounds; no per-chat DB/vector copies
Only a successful maintenance result with closed-or-absent turn, no durable save entries, accepted preparation and unchanged wake may mark an entry quiescent
The single frontend loop owns each entry revision; request arrival/completion invalidates quiescence, and stale maintenance results cannot restore it
Do not retire pending or actively borrowed entries. Do not periodically schedule confirmed quiescent entries. Retirement discards only in-memory cursors
Original multi-owner publication, full read/certification domains, search/ranking and final delivery gates remain unchanged
checks: Lean stale-result and pinned-entry retirement laws, actual declaration connections and standard ContractAudit
Native durable-file quiescence checks and authenticated frontend churn beyond its existing registry bound, with re-registration and unchanged private state
Then ordinary eight readers and eighty writers followed by eighty fresh readers, 5 KB then 50 KB; stop on failure
